methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multicenter study (13 Turkish centers), 118 HER2+ MBC patients enriched for PFS≥36 months. Multivariable logistic regression and Cox modeling. However, deliberately restricted to long-term responders introducing severe selection/survivor bias and immortal time bias. Time-dependent endpoint (NED) modeled as fixed covariate, violating Cox assumptions. Wide confidence intervals reflect small event count relative to covariates. Authors acknowledge these limitations appropriately.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective multicenter cohort of long-term responders. Clinical relevance moderate: NED associated with prolonged PFS (131 vs 66 months) in highly selected enriched population. LoE 2b (retrospective cohort) with major selection bias.

reporting_quality.justification: Excellent STROBE adherence: detailed baseline characteristics, clear endpoint definitions, statistical methods including assumption testing. Comprehensive discussion of limitations. However, data sharing not mentioned; institutional data not publicly accessible.

novelty_literature.justification: NED as response state in HER2-positive MBC explored in prior studies (16-44% NED rates). Current contribution is characterizing NED in multicenter real-world Turkish cohort—incremental regional population-specific study rather than new discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written, clearly organized with excellent acknowledgment of methodological caveats (survivor bias, immortal time bias, overfitting risk). Figures effectively display PFS separation by NED status. Appropriate cautious tone given limitations.

key_strengths: Multicenter real-world cohort from 13 Turkish centers providing practical data on long-term responders
Clear PFS/OS separation by NED status (131 vs 66 months)
Comprehensive multivariable analysis adjusting for clinicopathological factors
Excellent transparency regarding methodological limitations and survivor bias
key_concerns: Severe selection bias: restriction to PFS≥36 months excludes early progressors, making results non-generalizable to first-line populations
Immortal time bias: NED is time-dependent response state but modeled as fixed covariate in Cox model; estimates are associative only, not causal
Small event count (25.5% progression in NED group, 49.2% in non-NED) with wide CIs; multivariable models likely overfitted
No external prospective validation; findings require time-dependent/landmark analyses in broader populations
Heterogeneous local radiologic interpretation without central review; potential NED misclassification
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-conducted real-world study appropriately emphasizing hypothesis-generating nature. Severe selection bias and immortal time bias restrict to tier 3. Major revisions should: (1) reframe findings as associative markers in highly selected populations only, (2) recommend time-dependent analysis in future prospective work, (3) clarify that results do not apply to first-line unselected populations.
